fatal_errors: The proposed silicon-doping intervention does not reconstruct the demonstrated 30% AlFeNiCoCr high-entropy-alloy binder and spark-plasma-sintering strategy.
No prior evidence is cited for silicon-assisted densification or protection against the relevant liquid plating metal.
The proposed liquid-metal test uses an unspecified copper-based bath rather than molten aluminum at 700 °C, so it does not evaluate the target service environment.
The claim that segregated silicon will form a protective silicate glass during liquid-metal immersion is unsupported and conflates oxidation protection with liquid-metal corrosion resistance.
explanation: The hypothesis broadly addresses lower-temperature densification, mechanical integrity, oxidation, and liquid-metal corrosion, and it offers measurable comparisons and a nominal falsification rule. However, it misses the target intervention: an AlFeNiCoCr high-entropy-alloy binder that becomes fluid during SPS, fills pores, and optimizes density at 1500 °C. It also misses the decisive processing window and failure boundary—vacuum SPS at 50 MPa with a 5-minute hold, optimum performance at 1500 °C, and binder overflow with increased porosity at 1600 °C. The proposed mechanism is only partly plausible for oxidation and is not established for molten-metal corrosion. Its experiment includes useful density, microscopy, mechanical, oxidation, and penetration measurements, but lacks a silicon-content and temperature matrix, an SPS/process-matched control, the relevant molten-Al exposure for up to 12 days, and the target wear assessment. Comparison against a >2300 °C pure-ZrB2 body processed by a fundamentally different route also confounds composition and processing. With no cited supporting evidence and speculative performance claims, this is not an evidence-supported alternative.
